text:
Predicates:
Invertebrate(x) ::: x is an invertebrate.
Vertebrate(x) ::: x is a vertebrate.
Backbone(x) ::: x has a backbone.
Reproduce(x) ::: x reproduces by male-and-female mating.
Bee(x) ::: x is a bee.
QueenBee(x) ::: x is a queen bee.
Harry(x) ::: x is Harry.
Premises:
∀x (Invertebrate(x) ⊕ Vertebrate(x)) ::: Animals are either invertebrates or vertebrates.
∀x (Backbone(x) → Reproduce(x)) ::: All animals with backbones reproduce by male-and-female mating.
∀x (Vertebrate(x) → Backbone(x)) ::: All vertebrate animals have a backbone.
∀x (Bee(x) → ¬Reproduce(x)) ::: All bees do not reproduce by male-and-female mating.
∀x (QueenBee(x) → Bee(x)) ::: All queen bees are bees.
Harry(harry) ::: Harry is a bee.
Conclusion:
(Vertebrate(harry) ∧ Backbone(harry)) ⊕ ¬(Vertebrate(harry) ∨ Backbone(harry)) → (¬Invertebrate(harry) ∧ ¬QueenBee(harry)) ::: If Harry is either both a vertebrate and an animal with a backbone, or neither a vertebrate nor an animal with a backbone, then Harry is neither an invertebrate nor a queen bee.
